paper_id: From Image to Imuge_ Immunized Image Generation
title: From Image to Imuge: Immunized Image Generation
motivation: Existing fragile watermarking fails under real-world benign attacks like JPEG compression—images become unrecoverable after social media compression
problem_framing: Image self-recovery as joint encoder-localization-decoder pipeline: immunized image must survive compression yet enable tamper localization and content recovery
key_insight: Encoder spreads coarse content representation into ambient areas via residual image R, enabling decoder to reconstruct originals from tampered regions
method_signature: U-Net encoder+verifier+decoder trained with GAN, parameter-less noise layer simulating JPEG/scaling/clone attacks, progressive recovery from low-to-high resolution
evaluation_criteria: L-PSNR in tampered regions; BCE for localization; SSIM for visual quality; user study comparing fidelity vs inpainting
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Without verifier and discriminators, Imuge fails completely (L-PSNR drops from 27.43 to 13.16); larger tampers degrade recovery quality; plain areas need extra residual patterns
evidence_for_taste: Imuge fails to conduct content recovery
we do not compare Imuge with the previous fragile image self-recovery schemes
we find that the ℓ2 distance is better
the failure of precise tamper mask prediction always happens
the schemes are only tolerant to a typical kind of attack
thinking_moves: 把传统watermarking的不可逆失真问题重新frame成对抗攻击下的图像恢复问题
从网络训练耦合问题出发,提出task decoupling解决梯度相互干扰
观察到decoder特征比encoder特征包含更丰富的缺失区域信息,设计local feature sharing复用浅层特征
把真实世界攻击分类为malicious tamper和benign attack两类,提出参数无关噪声层统一模拟
